heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 can print Prusament PC Blend at speeds up to 143 mm/s capped by a 12 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. However, successful printing requires an external draft enclosure and disciplined bed adhesion strategies because the A1's open frame and 100°C bed ceiling fall just below ideal polycarbonate thermal thresholds.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with Magigoo PC or PVA Glue Stick release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 12 mm³/s in the filament profile to cap print speed at roughly 143 mm/s and avoid hotend under-extrusion.
Force Bed Temperature to 100°C across all layers and Hotend Temperature to 275°C.
Enable a 10 mm outer brim with 0.0 mm Brim-object gap to mechanical anchor edges against warp stresses.
Turn off regular layer cooling fans (0%) and restrict maximum cooling to 20% strictly for overhangs below 25 seconds layer time.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner lifting and severe warping from build plate
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: The A1 bed hits a maximum of 100°C, slightly below the PC glass transition temperature, combined with cool ambient room drafts.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of glue stick or Magigoo PC, add a 10mm mouse-ear/brim, and place a physical draft tent over the printer.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Interlayer cracking and splitting along Z-axis
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling airflow or ambient drafts chilling the extruded beads prematurely before polymer bonding occurs.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Set part cooling fans to 0%, enable the Draft Shield feature in OrcaSlicer, and keep ambient printer space warm.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rough surface finish, frothing, and excessive stringing
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Prusament PC Blend is hygroscopic and has absorbed ambient moisture, flashing into steam during extrusion at 275°C.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Bake the spool in a dedicated filament dryer at 80°C for 8 to 12 hours prior to printing and print from a dry box.

faq.question: Can I print Prusament PC Blend reliably without an enclosure on the Bambu A1?
faq.answer: Small parts under 50 mm can succeed open-air with a brim, but medium to large components will warp or delaminate without a draft shield or external enclosure tent.

faq.question: Does Prusament PC Blend require a hardened steel nozzle on the Bambu A1?
faq.answer: No, standard Prusament PC Blend is an unreinforced polymer blend and does not require hardened steel, meaning the stock stainless steel nozzle is sufficient.

faq.question: How do I mitigate the A1's 100°C bed limit when Prusament recommends 105-115°C?
faq.answer: Max out the bed at 100°C, allow the plate to heat-soak for 10 minutes before starting, utilize specialized PC adhesive, and eliminate room drafts.

faq.question: Can I use the Bambu AMS Lite to feed Prusament PC Blend?
faq.answer: Yes, standard PC Blend feeds through the AMS Lite, but the filament must be completely dry, and high-tension spool resistance should be monitored to prevent feed errors.
